title: Grom client manifest
description: One JSON file per client at the client-folder root. manifest_version 2 is the Standard Build shape: pipelines[] replaces the scalar pipeline_id + flat stage_map, because under the Standard Build every pipeline carries the SAME eight stage names and a flat name-keyed map cannot tell two campaigns apart. Version 1 stays valid and readable; Francesca, SK Skin and Alevere do not migrate.
x-standard-stage-canonical-note: At manifest_version 2 the stage names are FIXED, so the stage-to-canonical mapping is known in advance and is NOT recorded per client. This table is the single source for it: the mart seeder derives ghl_stage_map rows by joining pipelines[].stage_ids to this table, which is what removes the hand-written per-client SQL migration. Stages appended after Done are not in this table and map to NULL canonical (kept, excluded from the funnel). 'done' = sort 58, SHIPPED to grom-dashboard production 2026-07-27 (commit 82600ca) and verified on prod; 56, 57 and 59 remain free between treatment (55) and terms_sent (60).

allOf.$comment: v1 keeps the old contract verbatim.
v2 is the Standard Build. Keys must be PRESENT; values may still be null until harvest.

pipeline_id.$comment: v1 only. A single scalar cannot express one-pipeline-per-campaign. Superseded by pipelines[].

stage_map.$comment: v1 only. Flat, keyed by stage NAME, so two Standard Build pipelines (identical names) collapse into one indistinguishable map. Superseded by pipelines[].stage_ids. The canonical enum below is still the authoritative canonical-step vocabulary and is read by validate.mjs.

pipelines.$comment: v2. One entry per campaign/offer: its own lead form, landing page and booking calendar. NOT one per product; a fifteen-treatment menu behind one consult funnel is ONE entry.

key.$comment: Stable local identifier for this pipeline. Unique within the manifest.

funnel_slug.$comment: The value stamped by 01 as the funnel:<slug> tag, and the join key to LP tracking.

offer_price.$comment: The campaign's advertised offer price, written as the opportunity value at card creation. Number, never a string. Creating at zero is a defect: it makes the pipeline look empty and early drop-off look costless.

stage_ids.$comment: Stage NAME to GHL stage UUID. The eight keys are fixed and required (values may be null before harvest). Extra keys are permitted ONLY for stages appended after Done; they map to NULL canonical.

base_workflows.$comment: v2. Reserved numbering: each workflow owns its number for life, same number means the same job at every client, and gaps are information. A key that is ABSENT means that workflow is not built for this client (no deposits, external diary). Client-specific extensions are NOT recorded here; they live in the design docs at unused numbers.

published.$comment: Half of the deployment gate. The other half (trigger file non-empty) is asserted against exported workflow JSON, not from here.

lost_reason_ids.$comment: v2. The eight standard lost reasons, seeded as location-level options, mapped to their GHL ids. Every automated Lost write sets one. Do NOT create a custom lost-reason field; GHL's is native, is a merge tag, and is a filter on the stale-opportunity trigger.

per_cycle_fields.$comment: v2. Facts about THIS cycle, held on the OPPORTUNITY. Replaces the undecidable prose rule 'places a per-cycle value on the contact' with a declaration the validator can check against the account's actual opportunity fields. treatment_interest, cycle_index and amount_paid are always present.

staging_contact_field_id.$comment: The AI staging-slot exception. An AI agent CANNOT write an opportunity field; its only field-write capability is updateContactField. So an AI-captured per-cycle fact lands on a contact field named stg_<key>, and 01 or 03 copies it one-way onto the card. Write-only, not a source of truth, read by nothing else. Null when no AI captures this field.

enumerated.$comment: true for picklists keyed to registry product names (treatment_interest). Free text produces 'botox', 'Botox' and 'anti-wrinkle' within a week.

knobs.$comment: v2. The client-level settings that are machine-checkable. Copy, ladder wording and alert recipients are NOT here; they live in the design docs. The workflow set, its numbering, the removal matrix and the hygiene flags are FIXED and are not knobs at all.

touch_ceiling.$comment: Per-contact cap across ALL workflows, enforced by a shared counter field and checked before every send. Worst case across 01, 03, 04, 06, 07, 09 and 10 is about 26 touches without one.

decay_days.$comment: 10's opportunity_decay threshold. Validator asserts decay_days > ladder_length_days, so a 7-day decay cannot enrol a lead while 01 still has three touches left.

absence_close_days.$comment: 13's tail close: no future appointment plus this many days since last attendance sets Done.

treatment_payment_in_system.$comment: OFF by default. The pipeline tail is primarily MANUAL because Grom's data ends at booking and the clinic takes treatment payment on its own system. Turn on ONLY for a client who genuinely takes treatment payment inside the system; then 13 also triggers on payment_received, writes amount_paid, and owns the reprice. When off, the card keeps the advertised offer price and reporting must label it as advertised, not realised.

send_window.$comment: Quiet hours. Live sends have been observed at 23:22, 23:47, 02:55 and 03:20.

model.$comment: external suppresses 04 and 05 and requires 25. Alevere runs Cliniko, which already sends its own confirmations and reminders.

chat_booking_flow_workflow_id.$comment: v2. The booking agent MUST be a flow-builder bot: its logic IS a workflow, which is the only deterministic way to signal 'showed availability' (an add_contact_tag step immediately BEFORE the booking node). This id is what makes that checkable.
